**Applied phenomics and genomics in pigs for
the identification and use of new phenotypes
in breeding plans**

## Project overview

PigPhenomics investigated the application
of genomic and high-throughput phenotyping
approaches to identify and characterize
novel phenotypes in pigs.

The project combined genomic information
with molecular and phenotypic measurements
to investigate complex traits and explore
their potential applications in animal breeding.

## My research contribution

My research activities focused on the
analysis and interpretation of genomic
and metabolomic data, with particular
emphasis on molecular phenotypes and
their genetic architecture.

These activities included:

- Analysis of high-throughput metabolomic
  profiles in pigs.
- Genome-wide association analyses
  of molecular and intermediate phenotypes.
- Investigation of genetic factors
  associated with metabolite variability.
- Functional interpretation of genomic
  associations and metabolic pathways.

My contributions also included the
presentation of research results on
molecular phenotyping and the genetic
characterization of the pig metabolome.
